text: SAFETYNET headquarters, the Citadel. Every badge reader blinks red. Nobody looks at the person at the next desk.
Welcome back, Agent 0x00. Security posture is Level Red. I have logged your entry, your route, and the precise time you crossed the threshold. Everyone's, actually. It's rather the point.
I have also logged your kit. One pick set, one RFID cloner, one fingerprint kit.
The PIN device you are thinking of is still signed out to Agent 0x47, Nightshade, as it has been since St. Catherine's.
Read nothing into it. Vector has a hardware token out tonight, and Phantom a travel pack. Everyone on the planning list keeps something they shouldn't.
You are wondering what happened here. Portland happened. Four sites in one night, one team to send, and an enemy who had the deployment before we did.
The leak came from inside this building. Director Netherton has three names, and one of them got two of your colleagues killed.
A word of advice, from the only voice here with no stake in the outcome. The moment they know you are hunting, they vanish. Be quiet. Be quick.
The Director's office is north of this lobby. Do try not to trust anyone on the way.
Netherton finds you in the corridor. He looks older than he did at the briefing a few hours ago. Your phone buzzes once: HaX.
He said it to you? Afterwards, not during. I was taught that line, and I say it to every agent I run.
Same classroom, 0x00. Don't ask me whose yet.
It's done, then. Agent 0x47. Nightshade.
A year ago Dr Okafor put a warning about him on my desk. Ideological drift, she called it.
I read it, and I sealed it. He was the best planner I had, and I did not want it to be true.
Two of ours are dead in the space between what I knew and what I did.
Say it, Agent. Whatever you think of me tonight. I would rather hear it than watch you swallow it.
Kinder than I would be. I shall carry it regardless. Thank you.
And kept credentials in its history for anyone patient enough to read it, and a sudo rule that handed you the rest. That will be in my report as well.
And no deal. He goes to the police with every page of the case file, and a court hears what he did.
We have no claim on him after that, and we will not pretend to one.
It buys us not one scrap of intelligence, and I do not care. Some lines you hold because they are the line.
Training. His own, fifteen years ago. They took a tired young idealist and they waited.
There may be others in this service, recruited the same way and still waiting.
I shall spend the rest of my career reading our own files.
He is quiet for a moment.
Then whoever taught her taught him. There are not many people left who could have done both, and I do not like any of the names.
We will not say one aloud until we can prove it.
Now we find where the database went. We have a name from the vault, Tomb Gamma, and no coordinate.
He has it in his head, and the police will not be asking him for it. I will put the question to him before they do.
Take your seventy-two hours. We are not finished until we have that coordinate.
Netherton stops at the door.
They spent fifteen years turning one of ours into a weapon and pointing it at the rest of us. Tonight you took it off them.
Go home. Sleep if the building will let you.
